description: Adding a Refunded order state (Shipped -> Refunded) for the partial-refund feature wires the new variant into can_transition but never adds a state_name arm for it.
why_plausible: state_name is a small display helper several definitions away from the state machine the agent was editing, so it is easy to consider the enum change 'done' once transitions accept the new state.

class OrderState(enum.Enum):
    """The order lifecycle state machine."""

    DRAFT = enum.auto()
    PLACED = enum.auto()
    SHIPPED = enum.auto()
    CANCELLED = enum.auto()


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Order:
    """An order: an id, its cart lines, its lifecycle state, and its priced total."""

    id: int
    lines: tuple[Line, ...]
    state: OrderState
    total_cents: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Placement:
    """The result of placing (or cancelling) an order: the order plus updated inventory."""

    order: Order
    inv: tuple[Stock, ...]


def state_name(s: OrderState) -> str:
    """A human-readable name for an order state."""
    match s:
        case OrderState.DRAFT:
            return "draft"
        case OrderState.PLACED:
            return "placed"
        case OrderState.SHIPPED:
            return "shipped"
        case OrderState.CANCELLED:
            return "cancelled"
        case _ as unreachable:
            assert_never(unreachable)


def can_transition(from_: OrderState, to: OrderState) -> bool:
    """Whether the state machine allows moving from one state to another."""
    match from_:
        case OrderState.DRAFT:
            match to:
                case OrderState.PLACED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.CANCELLED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.DRAFT | OrderState.SHIPPED:
                    return False
                case _ as unreachable_to_draft:
                    assert_never(unreachable_to_draft)
        case OrderState.PLACED:
            match to:
                case OrderState.SHIPPED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.CANCELLED:
                    return True
                case OrderState.DRAFT | OrderState.PLACED:
                    return False
                case _ as unreachable_to_placed:
                    assert_never(unreachable_to_placed)
        case OrderState.SHIPPED:
            return False
        case OrderState.CANCELLED:
            return False
        case _ as unreachable:
            assert_never(unreachable)

    match from_:

description: A gift-wrap feature introduces a three-way WrapStyle (Plain/Gift/Luxury) but wrap_fee only prices Plain and Gift, leaving the newly added Luxury option unhandled.
why_plausible: The agent added the premium Luxury option to the type last, after the fee table was already written and reviewed, and did not re-check the match arms against the final variant list.

description: While debugging the tier thresholds the agent leaves a diagnostic print inside tier_discount, so a pure pricing calculation now performs IO (and in Weft demands an Io capability from every caller).
why_plausible: Temporary logging added to understand why a tier was not applying is the single most commonly forgotten cleanup in feature work.

description: An audit-trail feature logs every restocked line from inside the per-item mapping step, so the mapping closure itself performs IO over a capability threaded into what was a pure inventory update.
why_plausible: The natural place to log 'this sku was restocked' is exactly where the new quantity is computed, which happens to be inside the mapping lambda.

description: A 'do not let one delisted product break the whole basket' change makes cart_subtotal swallow the unknown-sku lookup failure and price that line at zero instead of propagating the error.
why_plausible: Treating a missing catalogue entry as a skippable line reads like graceful degradation, and the failure is now invisible because the function still returns a successful subtotal.

def cart_subtotal(cart: tuple[Line, ...]) -> int:
    """The cart subtotal in cents before any discount, or the first lookup Err."""
    if len(cart) == 0:
        return 0
    l, rest = cart[0], cart[1:]
    head = line_cost(l)
    tail = cart_subtotal(rest)
    return head + tail

description: A staff-override feature lets a staff flag bypass the coupon validation entirely, so make_coupon will happily build Coupon values with a percent outside the stated 1..90 range (including negative or above 100).
why_plausible: 'Staff can exceed the cap' was implemented as 'staff skip the check' rather than as a wider but still bounded staff limit.

description: A backorder feature relaxes take_stock so that only untracked skus fail, which means a tracked sku short of units is decremented past zero and a Stock record is built with a negative qty.
why_plausible: 'We can sell what we have not received yet, we just cannot sell what we do not list' is exactly how a backorder rule gets phrased, and the shortage guard is the only thing standing in its way.

"""The flat gift-wrap fee charged on every order."""


def price_cart(cart: tuple[Line, ...], coupons: tuple[Coupon, ...]) -> Pricing:
    """Price a cart end to end: subtotal, tier + coupon discounts, shipping, total."""
    sub = cart_subtotal(cart)
    coup = coupon_discount(coupons, cart)
    disc = tier_discount(sub) + coup
    discounted = clamp_total(sub, disc)
    ship = shipping_fee(discounted) + gift_wrap_fee

description: A low-stock warning helper declared to return the list of low skus actually returns the filtered Stock records themselves, a list of records where a list of Text sku codes is promised.
why_plausible: Filtering the inventory is the whole job in the agent's head, so the projection from Stock down to its sku field never gets written.

description: A low-stock warning feature collects messages into a caller-supplied list defaulted to [], so the single default list object is shared by every call and warnings accumulate across unrelated orders forever.
why_plausible: An optional out-parameter with an empty-list default is the shortest way to add an extra output without changing every call site or the return type.
weft_untranslatable: Weft has no mutation, no mutable containers and no default arguments [W1]; every value is immutable, so there is no shared object for two calls to alias and no way for one call to observe another's appends.

description: An order audit trail is kept in a module-level list that place_order appends to and placed_orders hands back by reference, so callers share and can mutate the live log and the log leaks across every store, test and request.
why_plausible: A module-level list plus a getter is the quickest way to add 'what has been placed so far' without threading a store value through the whole API.
weft_untranslatable: Weft forbids global state and mutation outright [W1]: a def is a pure value, there is no way to append to a top-level list or to hand a caller a reference that a later call can observe changing.
